Earlier this week, Apple revealed that Siri AI usage limits will be implemented in iOS 27.3 and explained how iCloud+ increases those limits. Now we have a real-world example of what it looks like when limits are hit, and details on what counts toward those limits.

Here’s how Siri AI usage limits will work in iOS 27.3

Siri AI and select other AI features will begin having usage limits in iOS 27.3 for advanced tasks.

This is standard practice with other AI services like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude because these tools rely on server-based models rather than running entirely on-device.

Here’s an example from the iOS 27.3 beta showing what it looks like when you hit your Siri AI daily usage limit. Per Ben in a post on X:

In a follow-up post, Ben clarifies that complex questions did stop working shortly after posting. As expected though, basic requests continued to work as usual—they don’t have a usage limit.

One question that Apple hasn’t made clear is what qualifies as a complex or “advanced” Siri AI request. The company shares just two examples of something advanced:

  • “Text Mark the address for Annika’s party, and tell him what time we need to leave from home to make it on time.”
  • “Add a summary of my San Francisco trip note to this email draft.”

Top comment by Phillip

really disappointing to see Apple embedding the AI scam into their devices and services. Siri has been so easy to disable and ignore for the last 15 years but in the last few years as Apple has bought more and more into the AI scam they're shoving it deeper into their ecosystem and making it more and more of a hassle to disable and ignore

But leaker pdfu has discovered exactly the instructions Siri AI follows to determine whether a request counts as basic or advanced. In a post on X he outlines the parameters for requests deemed “advanced.”

Siri AI will check the request against this list, and if it involves any of these, it’s deemed “advanced.”

  • uses information from one app, from what is on screen or from a message, in a different app, or needs a result from one step used in a different step or app (such as a looked-up fact typed into a field)
  • contains two or more separate asks in one sentence, even in the same app (extra details of one action, such as a cc or a time, are still one ask)
  • asks about or summarizes the content of a photo, a camera view or an attachment (editing, searching and albums are fine)
  • deletes, archives, junks, moves, marks or changes a set (all, every, these or a whole category) of the user’s emails, notes, reminders, messages, photos, files, contacts or events
  • sets a device action or a notification to run on a time or trigger (not alarms, timers, reminders or calendar events), notifies someone when a person arrives or leaves, or builds or edits a Shortcut or automation
  • is deep research or a multi-step task done on the user’s behalf
  • asks you to compose or create new content (a story, poem, essay, plan, recipe, image, or an email or message from a topic rather than wording the user gives), or to rewrite in a tone other than friendly, professional or concise

    • It would be helpful if Apple publicly documented these guidelines for users. But perhaps after iOS 27.3 ships and usage limits are fully implemented, we’ll get more detail from the company.

    What do you think of Siri AI’s parameters for advanced requests in iOS 27.3? Let us know in the comments.
